objective: Test assumption A97 (the owner's reading 'Distance is the only form of information'): do the pairwise bond distances of a not-all-equal base, read from its allowed states, determine those states? Exhaustive census for n <= 6, sampled n = 7; unsigned, signed and full-bond-set variants. Serves G1 and G16. Challenges A97.
status: Complete 2026-11-17 (Successful; refereed R1, corrected): which distance is meant decides it. Pairwise bond distance does not determine a not-all-equal base's allowed states (fails at four distinctions; at six, 10,012 tables for 97,248 bases), and which sets are bonds does not repair it; how often two distinctions differ in the allowed states determined every base tested through six and every sampled one at seven (the referee's reading, recomputed; computed). The first reading, that each bond with its excluded joint states is needed and A97 survives only with orientation, is withdrawn (Block): it also needed two-place ties counted as bonds. A97 under challenge, with the owner's answer (no direction; an order with nothing skipped).
stop_rule: One frozen census and its read-out; A97 status set; referee hand-off; report.
title: Is distance the only form of information: bond-distance tables of not-all-equal bases
